purpose: Repeat the paired/native-fp64 sanity measurements after user reported GPU contention; unchanged code/inputs/buffers/block size.

methodology.aggregation: Median of three seven-sample CUDA-event medians; round ranges reported separately
order: canonical then mixed, repeated three times
paired then native64-series then native64-library in each process
methodology.serialization: Existing /tmp/fluxbridge-gpu.lock; Nsight started only after all six timing processes exited
methodology.telemetry: 200 ms nvidia-smi samples during timing runs; no clock/cache control; precheck had no active compute processes

limitations: Kernel-only, preallocated 28-output particle/tetrahedron interaction; excludes preparation, search, assembly and transfer
Final tensor accumulation/output remains fp32 for all three controls
No numerical source changed; prior independent accuracy checks were not repeated; million-pair finite/agreement/graph checks repeated in every run
No exclusive GPU reservation or clock locking; desktop activity remains possible. Ranges reflect observed repeatability, not ideal hardware limits
Nsight replay timings are separate from ordinary warm/graph event timings
conclusion: Mixed paired throughput improves to 231.6 million pairs/s; native fp64 remains approximately 2.96x slower canonical and 3.87x slower mixed for identical seed formulas. Whole-core native fp64 replacement is not a speed shortcut on this device.
